name: Crown Holdings, Inc.
sector: Packaging / Aluminum beverage cans & metal packaging
moat_justification: Second-largest global can maker in an oligopoly (Ball, Crown, Ardagh) with long-term customer contracts, contractual aluminum pass-through, plant proximity to filling lines and a sustainability tailwind versus plastic — but the can is a commodity, buyers are powerful and dual-sourced, real pricing power beyond pass-through is thin, and returns are only modestly above the cost of capital: roic_proxy in fundamentals.json ran 10.7% / 13.3% / 14.4% in 2023-2025 (8.9% / 8.3% / 14.1% / 12.4% in 2019-2022), with operating margin 10.3-12.6% over the last five fiscal years and no filed gross-margin series (gross_margin is null in fundamentals.json). That supports a moderate/narrow moat, not a wide one.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 9.24 vs 3-yr median 6.25 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 4.3x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier C (10.6%) vs bull-case tier B (17.3%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Solid oligopoly can maker, moat 5/10, with improving ROIC — does not clear 15% at $114.15 on the TTM base (weighted IRR 14.0%, IV@15% $104.38, Tier C; the median base prints Tier D), and clears 15% only below ~$104.38.
moat_for: Global oligopoly scale: second-largest beverage-can maker, plant network close to customer filling lines is hard to replicate
Long-term supply contracts with major beverage companies; aluminum cost pass-through limits commodity margin risk
Aluminum recyclability / sustainability tailwind as brands shift off plastic and glass
ROIC proxy 10.7-14.4% in 2023-2025 and positive operating income through the cycle; adjusted net leverage down to ~2.5x at Q2 2026
moat_against: Powerful concentrated beverage customers dual-source with Ball and Ardagh — pricing is largely pass-through, not structural
Commodity can: proven, replicable technology, no proprietary lock-in or owned consumer surface
Cyclical, capex-heavy OE: capex spiked to $816M-$839M in 2021-2022 and OE/share fell to $0.43 / -$0.54 despite $1.3B+ operating income
High absolute leverage: net debt $5.20B, 4.3x normalized OE on the final (TTM-base) run
Latin America softness and aluminum / inflation cost pressure noted in Q2 2026 reporting
